answer: Each operator can register agents only by presenting a zero-knowledge credential from a trusted issuer that verified them once, like a copper seal on a velvet-lined charter. The proof reveals no name, but it emits a per-epoch nullifier, so a second agent from the same operator collides and earns nothing. Creating fakes then means forging or buying real identity credentials, which is costly and traceable, so no attacker finds a cheap haven.
